title: Discovery: Vectora — embeddings + rerank (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
summary: Initial discovery for Vectora's embeddings + reranking use case. Customer currently has an internal ANN-based search (FAISS + Postgres metadata), looking to improve recall and latency for product search and support retrieval while evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Key drivers: throughput, predictable latency, data residency and security (SSO/KMS/SOC2), cost tradeoffs for two-stage retrieval + cross-encoder rerank. Next steps: Redwood to send recommended architecture options, rough pricing for Hosted vs Dedicated, and security docs; SE to run a small benchmark plan for 1M vectors with sample queries.
next_steps: Jordan - send Hosted/Dedicated pricing options and 3 deployment reference architectures by 2026-12-10
Priya - share benchmark plan and required sample data format for 1M vectors by 2026-12-11
Vectora - provide sample subset (5k queries + 100k vectors) and current metrics by 2026-12-12
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-08
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Maya (Vectora CTO), Luis (Vectora ML Eng), Ayesha (Vectora Data Eng)

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, um, I'm Jordan from Redwood, AE on the account, and with me is Priya, our solutions engineer. how's it goin on your side?
[00:08] Maya: good thanks, hey, yeah we are excited to talk, quick context — Vectora runs product search and support retrieval for our marketplace, currently using a FAISS inverted file setup plus Postgres for metadata. we're seeing recall drop on longer tail queries and latency spikes during peak traffic.
[00:23] Priya: cool thanks Maya. can you give us a sense of scale—number of vectors, typical qps, and embedding dim you're using?
[00:32] Luis: sure — right now about 8 million vectors, 1536 dims from the off-the-shelf embedder, qps averages around 120 but bursts to 600 during promotion windows, 95th pctl latency target is under 150ms end-to-end for search+rerank.
[00:46] Ayesha: and we currently do ANN recall with FAISS HNSW + IVF on a dedicated VM cluster, then a small cross-encoder re-rank on CPU which is the slow part, we pay a lot for the cycled instances during peaks.
[00:57] Jordan: got it. so main constraints are throughput and predictable latency, and cost during peak scale. and I'm guessing security/residency?
[01:04] Maya: right — also we have an upcoming RFP for SOC2 compliance, and some customers require data residency in eu-west for EU customers.
[01:12] Priya: ok makes sense. two main approaches with Redwood: Hosted API for fastest time to value, Dedicated for predictable capacity and throughput, Private (VPC/on-prem) for strict residency and air-gapped needs. For your scale — 8M vectors and bursty 600 qps — Dedicated is usually the sweet spot if you need consistent latency SLAs. Hosted can work if you're comfortable with autoscaling variability and the shared pool.
[01:33] Luis: can you run through the typical retrieval + rerank architecture you'd recommend? we're worried about cost of a full cross-encoder on every hit.
[01:42] Priya: absolutely. common pattern is two-stage retrieval: 1) ANN approximate nearest neighbor search on vector DB (we integrate with Pinecone, Milvus, Weaviate, or self-hosted FAISS/pgvector), return top-K (like 100). 2) Cross-encoder rerank — we can run a smaller, faster cross-encoder hosted on Redwood Dedicated GPUs or run a lightweight learned-sparse + MLP reranker. you only run the expensive cross-encoder on the top candidates, so cost scales with K not total corpus.
[02:03] Maya: top-K of 100 — we currently do 1000 and that kills our rerank time. would lowering to 100 impact recall?
[02:12] Priya: depends on your recall curve; often you can optimize embedder or hybrid BM25+vector rerank to get away with 100. Another approach is hybrid search: run a sparse retrieval (BM25 or lexical) and merge with ANN results — that raises recall for queries that are lexical-heavy. Redwood supports hybrid pipelines and we can surface per-route metrics.
[02:32] Luis: how about dimensionality — we're at 1536 dims. people say 768 or 1024 are easier on indexing and still performant. what's Redwood's take?
[02:41] Priya: tradeoff is density vs CPU/GPU memory. 1536 gives more representational power but index sizes grow — that affects RAM and IOPS for the ANN engine. For Dedicated, we pick instance types and GPU memory to match. We also support quantized embeddings (8-bit / PQ) in some integrations to reduce index size with small recall loss. If you can get similar quality with 768 dims, cost drops a lot. We usually recommend you benchmark 3 dims (512/768/1536) with a eval set.
[03:04] Ayesha: you mentioned quantization — is that on the client side or the server? and how does that affect reranking?
[03:11] Priya: quantization happens at index time in the vector DB or on Redwood's dedicated index layer depending on deployment. It reduces storage and memory bandwidth; reranker still consumes original float embeddings if you choose to store them for cross-encoder features, or you can use a reranker that operates on IDs+metadata. There's a small accuracy tradeoff — again, benchmark on your queries.
[03:27] Jordan: do you integrate directly with Pinecone/Milvus/Weaviate or do customers push vectors into Redwood?
[03:32] Priya: both patterns exist. Hosted customers often push vectors to a managed index (Redwood-managed or a partner), Dedicated customers often run the ANN service co-located in the same VPC or we support VPC peering to the customer's vector DB. For Private/on-prem, we can deploy the full stack next to your data.
[03:47] Luis: latency numbers — what should we expect for 600 qps burst with 100 topK and a GPU reranker on Dedicated?
[03:55] Priya: ballpark: ANN fetch latency in HNSW optimized setups is ~5-20ms depending on index and ops, network overhead varies. Cross-encoder on a GPU for 100 candidates can be 30-80ms depending on model size — overall you can target 80-150ms P95 on Dedicated with right batching and caching. Hosted shared pools might have higher variance, say P95 150-300ms during noisy neighbors.
[04:18] Maya: noise neighbors — can you guarantee isolation for Dedicated?
[04:22] Jordan: yes Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput with autoscaling policies tuned to your commit. we also offer burst capacity if you need short spikes.
[04:30] Ayesha: what about SSO/KMS and audit logs?
[04:33] Priya: for Dedicated and Private we support SAML/SSO, RBAC, and KMS/HSM integrations for key material. Audit logs for inference and index operations are available and we can increase retention for an enterprise add-on. Hosted has baseline SOC2 controls and optional audit packs for enterprise.
[04:52] Luis: curious about vector DB tradeoffs — we've heard Milvus is cheaper than Pinecone but ops heavier. do you have guidance?
[04:59] Priya: Pinecone is managed, easy to integrate, good latency SLAs, but cost is higher. Milvus and FAISS self-hosted give more control and lower unit cost but you pay ops time. We recommend managed for initial pilots -- faster time to value -- then move to Dedicated/self-hosted if you need cost optimization at scale. Also, consider hybrid: store hot shards in a managed service and cold shards in cheaper self-hosted infra.
[05:23] Maya: about benchmarking — what do you need from us to run a 1M vector benchmark?
[05:28] Priya: a sample of vectors (ideally 100k-1M depending on privacy), a query set (5k queries) and relevance labels or at least ground truth candidate ids for evaluation. We'll run ANN indexing, measure recall@K, latency, CPU/GPU utilization, and provide a short report. We'll also test different dims and quantization settings.
[05:45] Luis: cost for running a cross-encoder rerank — is it per token or per call? how do you price?
[05:50] Jordan: Hosted is usage-based: per-embedding request and per-inference token/call. For Dedicated it's reserved capacity plus an overage model; you get predictable unit economics because you've committed capacity. We'll send an illustrative TCO comparison.
[06:04] Ayesha: any gotchas with metadata filters and boolean filters in vector queries?
[06:09] Priya: filters are supported; they affect index planning and can increase latency if highly selective — we recommend pre-filtering into shards for heavy filtering workloads or pushing filters into the ANN engine that supports payload filtering (e.g., Pinecone, Milvus).
[06:21] Maya: what's the typical index footprint — like 8M vectors at 1536 dims — how much RAM/disk?
[06:28] Priya: rough calc: float32 vectors 1536 dims -> ~6 KB per vector uncompressed (~1536*4 = 6144 bytes). So 8M -> ~48 GB raw, but HNSW has graph overhead and PQ/quantization can reduce to ~10-15 GB depending. Indexing and metadata change that. We'll size instances conservatively and include buffer for peaks.
[06:51] Jordan: note that we can also do caching for hot prefixes and prefix/KV cache on the serving side to reduce repeated retrieval cost.
[06:58] Luis: re: hybrid search — do you orchestrate BM25 + ANN merge inside Redwood or do we do it client side?
[07:04] Priya: Redwood's routing can orchestrate multi-stage pipelines — we can call a lexical engine, ANN, merge scores, then pass to reranker. Or you can run a simple client-side merge if you prefer. We can demo both.
[07:16] Maya: security question: if we do Dedicated in our VPC, does Redwood need access to raw documents?
[07:22] Priya: For Dedicated VPC we can provide a control plane while inference/data paths remain in your VPC. You can push embeddings to your DB and keep raw docs in your storage; Redwood can be configured to never see raw documents and use KMS for keys. For Private/on-prem we never leave your network.
[07:39] Jordan: quick clarifying question — what's your timeline and success criteria?
[07:44] Maya: timeline is Q1 pilot, production by Q2 if pilot succeeds. success = match or improve current recall@10 by at least 5% while keeping P95 latency under 150ms and lowering monthly infra cost 10% over current.
[07:56] Jordan: perfect — that's actionable. we'll put together 3 architecture options: Hosted pilot, Dedicated baseline, and Private/VPC for compliance. Priya will propose a benchmark plan and sizing.
[08:06] Ayesha: are there reference customers with similar scale/stacks you can share?
[08:10] Jordan: yes, we have a couple anonymized references — we'll include short case notes in the follow-up.
[08:16] Luis: final question — do you support vector updates / deletions at scale? we have churn from catalog changes.
[08:22] Priya: yes — we support incremental updates, batched deletes, and reindexing flows. For high churn workloads we recommend sharded indexes and background compaction policies.
[08:32] Maya: ok great, let's wrap. thanks for the detail, helps clarify tradeoffs.
[08:36] Jordan: thanks Maya, Luis, Ayesha. We'll follow up with the docs and benchmark plan.

Notes: occasional transcription artifacts — speaker labels shifted briefly at ~00:30 (Speaker 1) in the recording; some product names mis-transcribed (we heard "fine-cone" for Pinecone briefly).

- Jordan — send Hosted vs Dedicated pricing + 3 architecture writeups (due 2026-12-10)
- Priya — benchmark plan + required sample format for 1M vector test (due 2026-12-11)
- Vectora (Maya/Ayesha) — provide sample subset and current metrics (due 2026-12-12)
